title: Perfect projection formula for reductions
statement:
Let $X,Y$ be schemes, $f:X\to Y$ a morphism, and $(A,I)$ the adic datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with $A$ commutative Noetherian, $P_n=A/I^n$ finite as a set and perfect in $D(A)$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Put $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ for $T=X,Y$ and use the ordinary, uncompleted derived categories of $A_T$-module sheaves. The coefficient identification $f^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$ is the canonical one of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]; use the operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and their K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Fix $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. The full isomorphism locus of the map $\pi_{f,K,P}$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map], for $P\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, is a thick triangulated subcategory containing every finite free coefficient sheaf $A_Y^{\oplus m}$. It contains every site-perfect complex [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]: here site-perfect means locally on the site isomorphic to a bounded complex whose terms are direct summands of finite free coefficient sheaves, with bounds allowed to depend on the covering object. For every $n\geq1$ the canonical pullback comparison $Lf^*(P_n)_Y\cong(P_n)_X$ identifies the projection map with an isomorphism
$$\pi_n:(Rf_*K)\otimes^L_{A_Y}(P_n)_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*K_n,\qquad K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_X}(P_n)_X.$$
Its inverse $\rho_n$ agrees with the signed-totalization inverse for a finite-projective resolution of $P_n$. These maps and inverses are independent of the chosen resolution and commute with quotient tower maps, compatible coefficient endomorphisms, and base change in the projection-formula square of [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-base-change-naturality]. For proper $f$, they also agree with the identity-compactification formula [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-identity-compactification].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] to the finite rings $P_n$ from [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Their constant sheaves are $(P_n)_T$, as also identified in [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction]. Thus the operations' required coefficient identification $f^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$ is supplied; it is compatible with every quotient projection. In this coefficient setting the projection map is the adjoint of the counit tensored with pullback by [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map]. The tensor and adjunction in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] are the ordinary ringed-topos operations, hence specialize to precisely these operations, rather than to completed tensor or completed pullback.

At $P=A_Y$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] identifies the projection mate with $1_{Rf_*K}$. Both functors in its statement are additive, since they are exact, so the map on $A_Y^{\oplus m}$ is the direct sum of $m$ identities, including $m=0$. This proves the finite-free base case with the actual tensor unit $A_Y$, not the discrete constant sheaf $\underline A$.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] for the two exact functors in the $P$ variable and their shift-compatible natural transformation. The displayed shift equation proves invariance of the isomorphism locus under integer shifts. On any distinguished triangle it gives a morphism of distinguished triangles, including the connecting arrow; [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] then proves closure under the third vertex whenever two vertices belong to the locus. For a retract $Q\xrightarrow{i}P\xrightarrow{r}Q$, $ri=1$, an inverse to $\pi_Q:F(Q)\to G(Q)$ is $F(r)\pi_P^{-1}G(i)$. Naturality gives both composites equal to the identity, so the locus is closed under retracts. Together with the zero case this proves that it is thick triangulated.

Let $P$ be site-perfect. For each object $V$ choose a covering $V_i\to V$ on which $P$ has a bounded finite-projective representative. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-restriction] to identify each restricted projection map with the corresponding map for the localized morphism $f_{V_i}$. The exactness and unit statements of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] apply to these ringed topoi as well. Each term of the representative is a retract of a finite free coefficient sheaf, so step 3's explicit retract calculation gives the projection isomorphism on that term and all its shifts. The stupid truncations of a bounded representative are connected by degreewise split short exact sequences whose quotients are its single shifted terms; [lem-weil-pbc-degreewise-split-derived-triangle] gives the distinguished triangles. Induction on the number of nonzero degrees using [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] proves the projection isomorphism on the representative. Finally local detection in the restriction lemma proves it for $P$. Each induction is finite on its own covering object; no uniform bound or global thick-generation claim is used.

proof.text:
Fix $n$. By [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] and [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], choose a bounded finite-projective $A$-complex $F_n^\bullet$ representing $P_n$ in degree zero. [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] identifies $A_T\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{F_n^\bullet}$ with $(P_n)_T$ for $T=X,Y$; each term is a retract of a finite sum of $A_T$. Thus $(P_n)_Y$ is site-perfect. The level-$n$ comparison $c_{f,n}:f^{-1}(P_n)_Y\cong(P_n)_X$ is supplied directly by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Its displayed projection compatibility
$$\pi_{X,n}c_f=c_{f,n}f^{-1}\pi_{Y,n}$$
shows that $c_{f,n}$ is linear for the coefficient identification $c_f:f^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$; no morphism from the full quotient tower to a constant tower is needed. Exactness of identified-coefficient pullback in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] then gives $Lf^*(P_n)_Y\cong(P_n)_X$. Step 4 now proves $\pi_n$, whose target is $Rf_*K_n$ by the definition of $K_n$.

The resolutions in step 5 are global finite-projective packages over $A_T$. [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-totalization] supplies mutually inverse total arrows on such a complex, so its $\rho_n$ equals $\pi_n^{-1}$. The projection mate is defined independently of a resolution, and uniqueness of an inverse proves resolution independence for $\rho_n$. Naturality in $P$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], applied to $(P_{n+1})_Y\to(P_n)_Y$, gives the quotient squares, and [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-base-change-naturality] gives the coefficient-operator and base-change squares. All are for the same canonical projection mate, and the coefficient comparisons of step 5 commute with the quotient maps because they are induced by the same constant-ring maps and the projections in [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Equivalently, once a forward square commutes, multiplying it by the two inverse maps gives the reversed square; no base-change isomorphism is required for this reasoning. For proper $f$ use [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-identity-compactification] to identify the formula and inverse with the identity-compactification ones. This restores the compatibility clauses of the master's first statement, not just its Detailed form.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For every $n$ there is a natural isomorphism

$$
(Rf_*K)\otimes^L_\Lambda\Lambda/I^n
\xrightarrow[\pi_n]{\sim}Rf_*K_n
$$

whose inverse is $\rho_n$. The families $(\pi_n)$ and $(\rho_n)$ commute
with the reduction tower, compatible coefficient endomorphisms, and base
change.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Choose a strict-perfect package $F_n^\bullet\to P_n$. Signed totalization
gives inverse arrows

$$
(Rf_*K)\otimes^LF_n^\bullet
\mathrel{\substack{\xrightarrow{\ \pi_n\ }\\[-2pt]
\xleftarrow[\ \rho_n\ ]{}}}
Rf_*(K\otimes^LLf^*F_n^\bullet).
$$

Because $P_n$ is constant, $Lf^*P_n=P_n$, and the target is $Rf_*K_n$.
The identity-compactification lemma shows that this is also the open/proper
compactification composite for proper $f$. The totalization lemma gives
$\rho_n\pi_n=1$ and $\pi_n\rho_n=1$. Uniqueness of an inverse makes the map
independent of the strict-perfect package. Tower, operator, and base-change
compatibility are exactly the preceding two lemmas. This expands the
finite-projective argument located at Tag `0944`.

blueprint_update.statement:
For fixed $f$ and $K$, the full subcategory of objects $P$ for which
$\pi_{f,K,P}$ of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map] is an isomorphism is a
thick triangulated subcategory containing every finite free $A$-module. In
particular, it contains every perfect complex, and for every $n$ there is a
natural isomorphism

$$
(Rf_*K)\otimes^L_\Lambda\Lambda/I^n
\xrightarrow[\pi_n]{\sim}Rf_*K_n
$$

whose inverse is $\rho_n$. The families $(\pi_n)$ and $(\rho_n)$ commute
with the reduction tower, compatible coefficient endomorphisms, and base
change.

proof.text:
For $P=A$ the map $\pi_{f,K,A}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map] is the canonical tensor identity, an
isomorphism; for a finite free $P=A^m$ it is the direct sum of finitely many
of these, so every finite free $A$-module lies in the full subcategory. The
subcategory is triangulated-thick: it is closed under shifts ($Lf^*$, $Rf_*$
and tensor are exact triangulated by
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and commute with the shift comparisons),
under cones (applying $u:P_1\to P_2$ to the projection-formula maps makes the
cones of the $\pi$'s fit into a distinguished triangle, and the
two-out-of-three property gives the claim), and under direct summands (an
idempotent splitting of $P$ gives one of the isomorphism). Hence it contains
every perfect complex, i.e. every object of the thick triangulated
subcategory generated by the finite free modules, and in particular every
$P_n$'s finite free resolution in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], giving the displayed isomorphism
$(Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*K_n$.

Choose a strict-perfect package $F_n^\bullet\to P_n$. Signed totalization
gives inverse arrows

$$
(Rf_*K)\otimes^LF_n^\bullet
\mathrel{\substack{\xrightarrow{\ \pi_n\ }\\[-2pt]
\xleftarrow[\ \rho_n\ ]{}}}
Rf_*(K\otimes^LLf^*F_n^\bullet).
$$

Because $P_n$ is constant, $Lf^*P_n=P_n$, and the target is $Rf_*K_n$.
The identity-compactification lemma shows that this is also the open/proper
compactification composite for proper $f$. The totalization lemma gives
$\rho_n\pi_n=1$ and $\pi_n\rho_n=1$. Uniqueness of an inverse makes the map
independent of the strict-perfect package. Tower, operator, and base-change
compatibility are exactly the preceding two lemmas. This expands the
finite-projective argument located at Tag `0944`.
